We are going to go to a quick break, but when we return, it is more regional qualifier Sydney. Welcome to Riftbond Basics featuring the ground rules. Riftbond is a trading card game based on the League of Legends universe in which the aim is to score eight victory points across two different battlefields. Points are scored by moving your own units onto one of the battlefields and conquering it or by holding it for more than one turn. The different car types in Riftbound are units, gears, and spells. To play these, you must pay an energy cost, which is shown in the top left corner of the card, as well as a power cost. Energy is obtained by exhausting runes. These come from the 12 card rune deck from which the top two cards are played for free at the beginning of each turn. If you exhaust your runes to pay energy, you must also pay a power cost for some cards. To do this, you simply place one of your runes bearing the symbol shown on the card under your rune deck. You can also use runes that are already exhausted for this. The domains of the runes and the cards you play in your main and sight deck are determined by your legend. Units that you play enter the board exhausted. This means they cannot move until they are readyed at the start of the next turn. Just like all other exhausted cards on your side, you initially play your units and gears into your base. There they are protected from combat. Gears can't get into combat. If you already control a battlefield, you also have the option to play your units directly from your hand onto it. This is where your units might comes into play. This is the number shown on the top right hand corner of the units. Might represents both the attack power and the defensive stat of your units. If a player moves units into an already occupied battlefield, combat stunts. Here, spells with action and reaction speed can be activated to deal damage or modify might. When combat occurs and no player wishes to activate any more spells or abilities, the total might of all units is added together and distributed amongst the opposing units. Players may decide for themselves which opposing unit they wish to damage. Once combat is over, any damage is healed by units that were involved and did not die. The game ends when a player reaches eight victory points, though this is not quite so easy to achieve. Whilst every other point simply requires conquering a battlefield to earn the eighth point, you must either have held a battlefield for one round or you score two points in the same round.
